root_cause.text: The function `iavf_config_rss_reg()` uses `<=` in loop conditions when the loop bound is the number of dwords (`rss_key_size/4` and `rss_lut_size/4`), causing an off-by-one access beyond the allocated memory and device register range.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states "Using `<=` accesses one element past the end" and the patch changes `i <= adapter->rss_{key,lut}_size / 4` to `i < adapter->rss_{key,lut}_size / 4`. The KASAN splat shows a slab-out-of-bounds read at an address exactly at the end of a 52-byte allocation.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix off-by-one errors in RSS key and LUT register programming loops to prevent out-of-bounds memory access.
intent_record.what: Changed loop conditions in iavf_config_rss_reg from `i <= adapter->rss_key_size / 4` and `i <= adapter->rss_lut_size / 4` to `i < adapter->rss_key_size / 4` and `i < adapter->rss_lut_size / 4`.
intent_record.how: Prevents out-of-bounds memory access by ensuring loops iterate only over valid 32-bit words within the rss_key and rss_lut arrays.

candidates.rationale: This loop condition uses <= instead of <, causing one extra iteration when i equals rss_key_size/4, leading to out-of-bounds access of dw[].
This statement accesses dw[i] with i potentially equal to rss_key_size/4 due to the off-by-one loop condition, causing out-of-bounds read and register write.
